Take-Two $TTWO has priced its highly ‌anticipated "Grand Theft Auto VI" ‌at $79.99 and will launch the game ​on November 19th https://t.co/jJke8ONHRt

GTA VI will hit $1B in pre-orders in its first hour on sale today.

But no one is looking at $SONY, the mispriced money printer on the biggest entertainment product in history.

The trade on game publisher $TTWO has been priced in for a while. The highest street PT is 15% upside. The $GME upside is also light given the game is confirmed to have no discs.

You see the world still looks at $SONY as a low margin console seller with a mature, memory shortage exposed product in PS5. But really, Sony is becoming a digital products business from PSN memberships and in-game purchases, a perfect set up around GTA 6. Despite being a diverse $115B conglomerate, it derives most of its revenue and profits from its video games business.

$SONY is going to print high margin revenue alongside $TTWO, getting a cut of ~70% (console market share) of every game pre-order today, game purchase, and the in game economy purchases that still make $TTWO bags 13 years later.

Sony’s own CFO said this point best:

“The increase in operating income was mainly due to an increase in sales of add-on content and network services, as well as the impact of foreign exchange rates.”

Plus there will be a massive flood in high margin new and re-activated PSN online memberships. Think about how many churned, non active PS5 owners will re-activate here for this game.

You might think is this trade priced in because Sony recently guided for 30% earnings growth for their gaming business this fiscal year. 

However, almost of that earnings growth guided is from a large impairment $SONY took on its Bungie deal (Destiny publisher). So the organic growth from this once in a generation gaming catalyst is not baked in. To further support this "not priced in thesis", GTA's history of delays would make building guidance around it a  risky play for management.

Now you should know this thesis is not about console sales by the way. Memory shortages have forced Sony to hike PS5 prices, hurting demand. However, I believe the demand for GTA 6 is so asymmetrical, there will be major price inelasticity this holiday season, and PS5 will exceed sales targets anyway. It doesn't really matter though because the margins are very low on the hardware, the key is the console as a wedge into the high margin digital subscription and purchases revenue. 

Overall I love the R/R as the business is cheap here at 16x forward, down 20% year to date and down 50% from ATHs. I computed the base case at around $30 (50% upside) which aligns with other analysts like TD and BofA, so the company does look to be genuinley cheap.

IV and expected move on options are super low, so I'm taking an options trade and you won't see Sony show up in any of my @joinautopilot strategies for this reason. Hope is that the market might begin to see what I do around this massive launch as more catalysts build and pre-order data drops.

$SONY just had a double beat on earnings and raised guidance. ADR is up nearly 3% overnight.

My favorite non AI idea, I think this notoriously conservative conglomerate is still heavily sandbagging generational sales and profit impact of GTA 6 for FY26 (ending March 2027).

- Q1 revenue $17.8B +8% in yen, 2% in dollars.
- Q1 operating income $3.0B. Up 40% in yen, 27% in dollars.
- Q1 net income $2.15B, up 20% in dollars.
- Full year operating income guide raised from $10.4B to $11.1B

My focus is on gaming, but all the other wonderful businesses look really strong across the board with guidance raises for all but one segment.

GTA VI launches November 19. 112 days out and it lands inside Sony's fiscal year. Sony just guided full year gaming revenue up to $29.4B against $31.1B last year and sees profit climbing massively.

They are guiding gaming to SHRINK in the fiscal year that contains the biggest entertainment launch in history, to which they are the second biggest beneficiary of.

They raised gaming operating income by $388M and listed the reasons as tariff refunds, foreign exchange, cost improvements. Not one word about GTA VI or a major upcoming title.

Meanwhile $TTWO already put $8.0B to $8.2B of FY27 net bookings in writing, up from $6.7B. The platform collecting 20-30% of every dollar of 70% of that guide has its own gaming revenue going DOWN year over year.

That is before PS Plus reactivations and new sign ups and before the in-game purchases of the online economy, which ships day one this cycle instead of taking a while to build up like it did for GTA V.

$SONY also says that memory has been secured for their forecasted console demand this year and they won't expect a further change to profitability (so they won't be hiking prices further). My personal expectation is that PS5's will be impossible to buy this Holiday season, and we could even see front-loading happen this quarter.

Again this is just not a huge concern because profits are being guided up to over 39% growth. Sony's gaming business is getting more profitable amid the memory crunch because of all the network services revenue where the margin is (games, subscriptions). 

Risks are real though an earthquake just hit Japan that is disrupting their semiconductor factory that is a driver of their second most profitable business, but they expect it to come back online in August. This happened too recently to get baked into guidance. Also currency risk is material.

I'm personally holding Jan calls that are inching towards ITM. Already up 100% as of earlier today. Don't see reason to sell yet as it doesn't seem the market is putting two and two together yet on the GTA thesis.

Stock has crushed the last month up 13%, mostly from rotation out of AI. Trading at just 17x guided earnings. Still down big from its November high with the biggest catalyst in the division ahead.

The world's greatest social arb trader is long $TTWO.

I have the exact same thesis, but took everything he taught me and went long the real mispriced GTA bet in $SONY, with the largest options trade I've ever made.

Chris is the goat, but think I've got the bigger upside here.

3 thematic trade ideas I'm either actively playing or looking at this fall. And none of them are AI infra.

1) Clean Energy

This one is a Democrats crush the midterms trade, and they're priced at 87%+ to take the house. Trump has been openly anti-solar. If Democrats take the House and/or Senate, sentiment could pop. Historically, we've seen solar stocks crush when dems make any kind of progress in elections debates etc. IV looks decently low on a few set ups there as we move closer.

Residential solar has been crushed with names like $FSLR, $ENPH priced for a no subsidy world. 

2) Drones

Bipartisan so midterms aren't as dangerous. Massive funding being allocated, almost every drone stock crushed its earnings and raised guidance. Supercycle continues, and politicians aren't standing in the way. China export controls, U.S. supply chain priorities and potential government stakes.

I personally like $LPTH a lot as well as the neoprime drone builders $AVAV, $KTOS, $AVEX.

3) GTA 6 

Biggest entertainment launch in history happening this November, and hype is going to build more and more. I'm long $SONY LEAPS here. Not saying there's no alpha for $TTWO bulls, but think it's more limited than $SONY in terms of expectations already being so high for that stock. I've posted about my thesis quite a bit.

mentions.text:
GTA VI will be out in less than 3 months. Sink or swing for Take-Two Interactive $TTWO?

BofA says there's 58% upside. They reiterate Buy with a $368 target against $233, off the back of the GTA 6 gameplay reveal that Netflix aired last week.

The funny part is in the risk section.

Since August 18, an anonymous account called CyberLeek has been posting GTA 6 clips, and the details look consistent with someone having a real playable build. Rockstar acknowledged it on the 26th.

But the same account is also promoting its own meme coin, so BofA's reasoning for why this probably isn't catastrophic is that the motive looks financial, and monetizing through a token is a less direct path than just distributing pirated copies.

The bull case includes "the leaker seems more interested in his shitcoin." You can't make this up.

On valuation, TTWO trades at 93x FY2026 EPS and 53x FY2027. I get that GTA Online is a machine, but I wonder whether it justifies that kind of built-in premium.

Not my type of setup, but interesting nonetheless.
